recent.title: Disclosure Day
recent.review: A slog. Spielberg moments are occasionally there, but it's held back by glacial pacing and just absurd character decisions. I'm not even sure the plot makes any sense at all if you follow it through. Truly "we have Arrival at home" territory. Bad guys occasionally oscillate from friendly negotiations to trying to murder our main characters back to lightly jostling. I don't even understand the villains' motivations at all to be frank, nor does it ever seem the two main characters are really needed at all and maybe just a proxy to show bad CGI animals? There are explanations there, but none of it really feels satisfactory. The religion/nun subplot thing was also pretty hammy and I could feel Spielberg winking at me every time it came up. Just a mess of a film and one I'd rank pretty low on one of my favorite director's catalog.

recent.title: Mortal Kombat II
recent.review: These movies are a guilty pleasure of mine. By no means a good film, maybe even a bad one, but I enjoy the Mortal Kombat world enough that I'll stay for the good stuff. Fights are pretty fun, though dare I say less creative than the 2021 venture? Special effects look like garbage (that scene where they slit Raiden's neck looks horrid and the dead pools looked like a Windows screensaver). Was nice it was an actual tournament this time and had some stakes to it. They did the millennial edgy thing where they killed Cole presumably due to backlash from the last film. I'm glad he's gone, but it's a little bit of an overcorrection, would have preferred he had zero screen time and died off screen. Thankfully no mention of the tattoos. I think this might have bombed so we might not get a 3, but its enjoyable enough, I'll keep hoping it happens.

recent.title: Obsession
recent.review: A nice fun romp. Two things really stuck out to me in this flick. Arresting cinematography and a really awesome score. Besides that, I was very whelmed. Entertaining and clever ending, but also one that was evident from a mile away. Nikki was stellar (and the hype was correct). Although the rest of the cast was just ok. Dragged a little bit at parts, but still, very happy to see this do well as an original picture and one with a reasonable budget. I would take 500 more of these over another Masters of the Universe or Predator: Badlands.

recent.title: Minions & Monsters
recent.review: Family movie-time. Went to the local Movie Tavern over the holiday with the kids. Always enjoy these. Minions and Monsters was very clever and silly. We delighted in all the different monsters and the bits that were tied into old cinema. Typical - lots of physical humor and really great animated sequences to bring it all together.

recent.title: An American in Paris
recent.review: Not a cohesive production. I didn't necessarily dislike it due to the musical nature. It is however, very disjointed. Also it really doesn't have a plot. I struggle a lot with a film like this that is inherently beautiful and is a breath of fresh air compared to what we often get in modern times. Ultimately though, I need to think about whether I actually enjoyed it. Mostly, no. Awkward, overlong musical sequences (and I hold this completely separate from the biggest offender, the 20 minute closing number, which is its own footnote.) Quote wise, there's a few doozies, but I think this one is what sums up this film for me: "Oh, she's an enchanting girl, Adam. Not really beautiful, and yet, she has great beauty." Probably will never watch this again, but I can't deny there were a ton of really great character moments.

recent.title: The 'Burbs
recent.review: Solidifying Dante as one of my favorite filmmakers, a fantastic little suburban satire. Weird thing is any time someone tries to goof on the suburbs, they just end up making it look cool (Edward Scissorhands, The Truman Show, etc.). A colorful cast of characters that all really add to the constant calamity around whether or not the newcomers are secret killers or just odd. The closed off nature of our little cul-de-sac mimics a single location film feeling and the physical humor comes in droves. The whole journey felt quirky and humorous. The ending felt a little rushed and/or indecisive. Not good or bad really, but just not as cohesive and tight as the rest of the film and really reeks of studio interference or rewrites or something (but I have no idea if that's the case.)

recent.title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
Galaxy Quest
recent.review: Not just a great Star Trek parody, also a fine film in its own right. Extremely funny bits that still cause belly laughs over 25 years later and definitively better than any actual Star Trek property since its release. Just a ton of whimsy and supremely rewatchable. The special effects are highly commendable splitting the line between the TV set aesthetic and the real world superbly. A comedy classic.

recent.title: The Fly
recent.review: A Cronenberg classic. Jeff Goldblum before he fully became "Jeff Goldblum". The chemistry with Geena Davis is delightful. The special effects are magnificent and disgusting, completely on-brand. Many unique and quintessential scenes such as the arm wrestling scene and the final showdown after snatching Veronica from the hospital and of course the teleportation sequences. This is a rewatch for me, but a rewatch far removed from the last time I saw it, probably over 20 years ago. Still completely works and it probably won't be another 20 before I watch it again.

recent.title: Masters of the Universe
recent.review: Convinced to go on $5 tickets to a 4DX showing (first one I've been to.) 4DX was pretty rad, this film was all over the place though. First off, 2.5 hours? Why? What are we doing here? This legit gets at least 1 more star from being 90 minutes. It wasn't all bad, but we've really suffered under the effects of millennial/Joss Whedon writing for far too long. Maybe people in the 50s thought this about 50s film by the time it was all over, who knows? Anyway it's competently entertaining, but far from good or well-executed. It wasn't as awful as the trailers made it out to be and that's the kindest thing I can say about it.

recent.title: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie
recent.review: A fun little comedy adventure completely layered with good bits. This feels like a film begging to be watched a few times to really catch all of them. The really surprising part though is the insanely great looking special effects. Floored by how this film looks. Some day hopefully I come across a behind-the-scenes that goes into more detail, but its crazy to say - this looks better than many modern big budget films. I've only ever really seen one bit from the web show (well represented here in a scene, the 'Wii Shop Wednesday' song), so maybe I didn't fully absorb the total context the first time through, but worthy of my time and will probably revisit soon.

recent.title: The Social Network
recent.review: Was too hard on this one when it first came out. It was like seeing a 9/11 film in 2003. The real events were too recent and in this case, I was also there in a sense because I started using Facebook as our school was one of the early adopters. Now, in the year 2026 it feels much more like a retrospective and I was able to more subtly enjoy David Fincher's direction and storytelling. Jumping between two legal proceedings and intertwining that with the story works really well and keeps a tension throughout. The score fit the awkward atmosphere with some neat understated industrial and synth tones.
